title: Declarative Attention
description: Read less KV. Move no KV. An interactive, explicitly simulated journey from an empty GPU to selective attention.

narration.title: An empty GPU
narration.text: Empty GPU. Compute on top. Memory below. The host coordinates; PCIe connects them.

narration.title: Weights arrive
narration.text: Weights cross PCIe and stay in GPU memory. Same GPU. Now it has a model to run.

narration.title: A long request
narration.text: The request arrives in four chunks. Each holds two thousand forty-eight tokens. The question and instructions stay in a smaller scaffold.

narration.title: Build the KV cache
narration.text: Prefill turns the request into keys and values. Those blocks now live in GPU memory. Keep an eye on their seats.

narration.title: Read everything
narration.text: Vanilla decoding reads all the cached context for the next token. Follow the colored packets. These are reads, not relocated blocks.

narration.title: Pay again, every token
narration.text: Another token, another full read. The previous response token is now cached too. In this long-context picture, memory traffic is the cost we are isolating.

narration.title: Declare where to look
narration.text: The model writes a focus declaration into its output. The engine parses it, then changes the read mask. Other chunks dim, but none leave their seats. Predict what the next step will read.

narration.title: Read less
narration.text: Now read the scaffold, chunk three, and the response so far. Fewer packets. A smaller bar. The same resident cache. Did we free any memory?

narration.title: What the paper measured
narration.text: The paper reports fifty-two percent fewer attended tokens for Gemma four, thirty-one B, averaged across decoding, with about one point three percentage points lower accuracy. That is not our next-token bar, and not a measured GPU speedup.

narration.title: Look around again
narration.text: Global attention makes every chunk available again. One full read to cross-check. Nothing needs to be fetched back from the host.

narration.title: Answer from what you know
narration.text: Local attention skips every context chunk. The scaffold and the accumulated response remain available. Our scripted example can now give its answer. Why is the read bar still above zero?

narration.title: The seats never changed
narration.text: Read less KV. Move no KV. The mask changed which cached bytes were read, not where they were stored. Save a comparison, try another focus, and decode one step. Notice what changes and what stays.
